'''Sawawachigi Shrine''' (佐波波地祇神社, Sawawachigi Jinja/Sawawakunitsukami Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Kitaibaraki City|ja|北茨城市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaibaraki City|qq=}}, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ibaraki Prefecture|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (minor shrine) of the {{ill|Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hitachi Province|qq=}}, with two shrines in the city considered its possible locations.

== Overview ==
This shrine is located on Mount Karakai in Ōtsu-chō, Kitaibaraki City. According to shrine tradition, during {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|qq=}}’s eastern campaign, his fleet was caught in adverse waves for several days. One night, the deity appeared in his dream, saying, "I am the deity of Sawawa. I have come to protect your ships. I will calm the winds immediately." Upon awakening, the winds had indeed calmed. Yamato Takeru dedicated offerings and enshrined the deity on Mount Sawawa. The shrine became revered as a protector of maritime traffic, earning the name "Karagai no Miya" ("Shrine of Returning from Tang").
In 1869, it was Ranked as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=}} but was later demoted to {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=}} in 1871. In 1880, it was reinstated as a gōsha.
=== Deities ===
The main deity is {{ill|Amahikata Kihikata no Mikoto|ja|天日方奇日方命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amahikata Kihikata no Mikoto|qq=}}. Other deities enshrined include:
- {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}}
- {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}
- {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=}}
- Hime Tatara Isuzu-hime no Mikoto
- Isuzuyori-hime no Mikoto
=== Grounds ===
The honden, built in 1727 during the Kyōhō era, is of the nagare-zukuri style with a copper roof. The former haiden, constructed in 1878, was dismantled in 2018, and a new haiden was completed in 2019.

=== Ofune Festival ===
The spring festival is held once every five years, known as the "Ofune Festival," spanning May 2–3. In 2017, it was designated an {{ill|Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|qq=}} by the Japanese government under the name "Hitachi Ōtsu no Ofune Matsuri."
=== Access ===
* From {{ill|Ōtsu Port Station|ja|大津港駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtsu Port Station|qq=}} (JR Jōban Line), walk 30 minutes east.

== Overview ==
This shrine is located on the slopes of Mount Shiobara in Hanakawa-chō, Kitaibaraki City. According to tradition, Yamato Takeru worshipped the Sawa deity here on his return journey from his eastern campaign. Initially located on Mount Sawa, about 4 kilometers northwest of the current site, the shrine was moved to the mountain summit in 1569 and later relocated to its present position on the slope.
=== deity ===
The enshrined deity is Amahikata Kihikata no Mikoto, also known as:
- Atatsukushinimikoto (阿多都久志尼命)
- Takemisakasawayanosonuminomikoto (速甕之多気佐波夜遅奴美神)
